papers/running-key/2012-Reddy-Knight-Dec.title: Decoding Running Key Ciphers
papers/running-key/2012-Reddy-Knight-Dec.author: Sravana Reddy; Kevin Knight
papers/running-key/2012-Reddy-Knight-Dec.notes: Canonical NLP attack on running-key ciphers; Bayesian/HMM decoding with an n-gram LM over both plaintext and keytext.

papers/misc/2017-Greydanus-Learning-the-.title: Learning the Enigma with Recurrent Neural Networks
papers/misc/2017-Greydanus-Learning-the-.author: Sam Greydanus
papers/misc/2017-Greydanus-Learning-the-.notes: Placeholder relevance: learned models of polyalphabetic machine ciphers.

papers/runic/2023-HistoCrypt-Runic-crypt.title: Runic cryptography in early epigraphic period (200-700)
papers/runic/2023-HistoCrypt-Runic-crypt.notes: Directly on runic cryptography in inscriptions; bears on whether the Liber Primus runic layer has historical cryptographic precedent.

papers/otp-unicity/2022-HistoCrypt-Unici.title: Unicity Distance of the Zodiac-340 Cipher
papers/otp-unicity/2022-HistoCrypt-Unici.notes: Computes unicity distance for a real unsolved-then-solved cipher. Method transfers directly to the LP derived-vs-pad question: how much ciphertext is needed before a decryption is uniquely determined.

papers/running-key/2020-HistoCrypt-Proje.title: The Use of Project Gutenberg and Hexagram Statistics to Help Solve Famous Unsolved Ciphers
papers/running-key/2020-HistoCrypt-Proje.notes: Gutenberg as a keytext corpus + hexagram (6-gram) statistics against unsolved ciphers. This is exactly the SKELETON lane's method; read for how they controlled false positives over a large corpus.

papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Cryptodiagno.title: Cryptodiagnosis of “Kryptos K4”
papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Cryptodiagno.notes: Methodology for diagnosing an unsolved short ciphertext without solving it - closest published analogue to LP's situation.

papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Massive-ML-C.title: A Massive Machine-Learning Approach For Classical Cipher Type Detection Using Feature Engineering
papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Massive-ML-C.notes: Cipher-type classifier over 50+ classical cipher types. Could be run on LP ciphertext as an independent instrument.

papers/misc/2022-HistoCrypt-New-Ciphers-.title: New Ciphers and Cryptanalysis Components in CrypTool 2
papers/misc/2022-HistoCrypt-New-Ciphers-.notes: Inventory of implemented classical cryptanalysis components; a source of instruments the repo does not currently vendor (cf. GAPS G-04).

papers/misc/2023-HistoCrypt-Encrypted-Ep.title: Encrypted epigraphy - the case of a mysterious inscription in the Neapolitan church of Santa Maria

papers/misc/2022-HistoCrypt-Deep-Learnin.title: Evaluating Deep Learning Techniques for Known-Plaintext Attacks on the Complete Columnar Transposition Cipher

papers/runic/2021-HistoCrypt-Upplandic-N.title: The Upplandic Non-Lexical Rune Stones: Ciphers or Nonsense?
papers/runic/2021-HistoCrypt-Upplandic-N.author: Victor Wase
papers/runic/2021-HistoCrypt-Upplandic-N.notes: Runic sequences that may be cipher or may be meaningless. This is the exact epistemic problem the Liber Primus poses and the only paper found that treats it in a RUNIC setting.

papers/ngram-scoring/2021-HistoCrypt-Dor.title: Experimental Analysis of the Dorabella Cipher with Statistical Language Models
papers/ngram-scoring/2021-HistoCrypt-Dor.author: Bradley Hauer; Colin Choi; Anirudh S. Sundar; Abram Hindle; Scott Smallwood; Grzegorz Kondrak
papers/ngram-scoring/2021-HistoCrypt-Dor.notes: Statistical LM analysis of a short unsolved cipher; how LM scores behave when the ciphertext is too short to be decisive.

papers/ngram-scoring/2023-HistoCrypt-His.title: Historical Language Models in Cryptanalysis: Case Studies on English and German
papers/ngram-scoring/2023-HistoCrypt-His.author: Béata Megyesi; Justyna Sikora; Filip Fornmark; Michelle Waldispühl; Nils Kopal; Vasily Mikhalev
papers/ngram-scoring/2023-HistoCrypt-His.notes: How LM choice (period/register/language) changes cryptanalytic scoring - bears on quadgram models applied to LP's archaic register.

papers/transcription/2022-HistoCrypt-Los.title: Lost in Transcription of Graphic Signs in Ciphers
papers/transcription/2022-HistoCrypt-Los.author: Giacomo Magnifico; Beáta Megyesi; Mohamed Ali Souibgui; Jialuo Chen; Alicia Fornés
papers/transcription/2022-HistoCrypt-Los.notes: Transcription error as a cryptanalytic confound - bears on GAPS G-03 (single-root transcription lineage).

papers/transcription/2021-HistoCrypt-Uns.title: Unsupervised Alphabet Matching in Historical Encrypted Manuscript Images
papers/transcription/2021-HistoCrypt-Uns.author: Jialuo Chen; Mohamed Ali Souibgui; Alicia Fornés; Beáta Megyesi
papers/transcription/2021-HistoCrypt-Uns.notes: Automated glyph reading from manuscript images; relevant to the parked per-rune re-transcription (PARKED P-1).

papers/corpora/2022-HistoCrypt-DECODE-Da.title: The DECODE Database of Historical Ciphers and Keys: Version 2
papers/corpora/2022-HistoCrypt-DECODE-Da.author: Mihály Héder; Beáta Megyesi
papers/corpora/2022-HistoCrypt-DECODE-Da.notes: The DECODE database - a corpus of historical ciphers and KEYS. A source of real key material and of cipher-type priors.

papers/nulls-interrupters/2023-HistoCryp.title: On the Combination of Cryptography and Steganography in 17th Century Germany
papers/nulls-interrupters/2023-HistoCryp.author: Eveline Szarka
papers/nulls-interrupters/2023-HistoCryp.notes: Historical combination of cipher and steganography incl. null/dummy symbols.

papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Rabenhaupt-E.title: Solving a Mystery From the Thirty Years’War: Karel Rabenhaupt ze Such´e’s Encrypted Letter to Landgravine Amalie Elisabeth
papers/misc/2021-HistoCrypt-Rabenhaupt-E.author: Eugen Antal; Pavol Zajac; Jakub Mírka

papers/misc/2023-HistoCrypt-Internationa.title: International Conference on the Voynich Manuscript 2022
papers/misc/2023-HistoCrypt-Internationa.author: Colin Layfield; René Zandbergen; Lisa Fagin Davis; John Abela; Claire Bowern; Michael Rosner; Lonneke van der Plas

papers/otp-unicity/2013-Ryabko-Vernam-ci.title: The Vernam cipher is robust to small deviations from randomness
papers/otp-unicity/2013-Ryabko-Vernam-ci.author: Boris Ryabko
papers/otp-unicity/2013-Ryabko-Vernam-ci.notes: **Top-tier for the derived-vs-true-pad question.** Quantifies how much a keystream may deviate from uniform before Vernam secrecy degrades, in terms of the keystream's entropy deficit. Gives a formal handle on 'a derived keystream is still effectively a pad up to N symbols'.

papers/running-key/2016-Ryabko-Informati.title: Information-Theoretical Analysis of Two Shannon's Ciphers
papers/running-key/2016-Ryabko-Informati.author: Boris Ryabko
papers/running-key/2016-Ryabko-Informati.notes: Information-theoretic treatment of the running-key/Vernam family; complements the Vernam-robustness result.

papers/otp-unicity/2024-Revisiting-the-U.title: Revisiting the Unicity Distance through a Channel Transmission Perspective
papers/otp-unicity/2024-Revisiting-the-U.notes: Modern re-derivation of unicity distance. Needed to state, for LP, how many runes must be right before a candidate decryption is uniquely determined rather than one of many.

papers/otp-unicity/2005-On-the-Unicity-D.title: On the Unicity Distance of Stego Key

papers/extreme-value/2012-Schwartzman-Mu.title: Multiple testing of local maxima for detection of peaks in 1D
papers/extreme-value/2012-Schwartzman-Mu.notes: **Directly applicable to keyspace sweeps.** Treats 'is this score peak real?' as a multiple-testing problem over local maxima, with FWER/FDR control. The repo's sweeps report best-of-N scores with no such control.

papers/extreme-value/2010-Peak-Detection.title: Peak Detection as Multiple Testing
papers/extreme-value/2010-Peak-Detection.notes: Companion to the above; the framework for turning a raw best-of-N maximum into a calibrated p-value.

papers/extreme-value/2026-Optimal-multip.title: Optimal multiple testing under family-wise error control: elementary symmetric polynomials

papers/anti-repeat/2015-Application-of-S.title: Application of Smirnov Words to Waiting Time Distributions of Runs
papers/anti-repeat/2015-Application-of-S.notes: **Directly on the LP2 anti-repeat filter.** Smirnov words = words with no two equal adjacent letters. Gives waiting-time / run-length distributions, i.e. the null model against which the observed ~83%% doublet suppression must be scored.

papers/anti-repeat/2019-On-enumerators-o.title: On enumerators of Smirnov words by descents and cyclic descents

papers/anti-repeat/2018-Enumerative-prop.title: Enumerative properties of restricted words and compositions
papers/anti-repeat/2018-Enumerative-prop.notes: Survey-grade enumeration of words/compositions under adjacency restrictions (Carlitz/Smirnov). Supplies the generating functions needed to compute exact expected doublet counts for a 29-symbol alphabet.

papers/anti-repeat/2001-Average-number-o.title: Average number of distinct part sizes in a random Carlitz composition

papers/anti-repeat/2023-Smirnov-words-an.title: Smirnov words and the Delta Conjectures

papers/otp-unicity/2010-NIST-SP800-22r1a.title: A Statistical Test Suite for Random and Pseudorandom Number Generators for Cryptographic Applications (SP 800-22 Rev 1a)
papers/otp-unicity/2010-NIST-SP800-22r1a.author: Rukhin et al. (NIST)
papers/otp-unicity/2010-NIST-SP800-22r1a.notes: The standard battery. Defines exactly what a randomness test CAN and CANNOT distinguish - the negative result matters here: passing SP800-22 does not distinguish a derived keystream from a true pad.

papers/otp-unicity/2018-NIST-SP800-90B-E.title: Recommendation for the Entropy Sources Used for Random Bit Generation (SP 800-90B)
papers/otp-unicity/2018-NIST-SP800-90B-E.author: Turan et al. (NIST)
papers/otp-unicity/2018-NIST-SP800-90B-E.notes: Min-entropy estimators for non-IID sources. Gives the estimators to apply to a candidate LP keystream to bound its entropy from below - the operational version of 'derived or true'.

theses/2002-Clark-Metaheuristic-Search-a.title: Metaheuristic Search as a Cryptological Tool
theses/2002-Clark-Metaheuristic-Search-a.author: John A. Clark
theses/2002-Clark-Metaheuristic-Search-a.venue: University of York, PhD thesis (White Rose eprints)
theses/2002-Clark-Metaheuristic-Search-a.notes: Book-length treatment of search-based cryptanalysis, including how to choose a cost function and what a failed search does and does not prove.

theses/2022-QUT-Security-analysis-of-shi.title: Security analysis of shift-register based keystream generators for stream ciphers
theses/2022-QUT-Security-analysis-of-shi.author: Matthew Beighton
theses/2022-QUT-Security-analysis-of-shi.venue: Queensland University of Technology, PhD thesis
theses/2022-QUT-Security-analysis-of-shi.notes: Keystream-generator analysis: how structure in a generated keystream is detected. The mirror image of the derived-vs-true-pad question.

papers/ngram-scoring/2011-Ravi-Knight-Ba.title: Bayesian Inference for Zodiac and Other Homophonic Ciphers
papers/ngram-scoring/2011-Ravi-Knight-Ba.author: Sujith Ravi; Kevin Knight
papers/ngram-scoring/2011-Ravi-Knight-Ba.notes: Bayesian decipherment of a real unsolved-class cipher. The prior/likelihood decomposition is what a principled LP scoring model would need instead of a bare quadgram sum.

papers/ngram-scoring/2013-Nuhn-Schamper-.title: Beam Search for Solving Substitution Ciphers
papers/ngram-scoring/2013-Nuhn-Schamper-.author: Malte Nuhn; Julian Schamper; Hermann Ney
papers/ngram-scoring/2013-Nuhn-Schamper-.notes: Beam search with n-gram LM scoring; gives the empirical relationship between LM order, beam width and success rate - i.e. how much ciphertext and how good a model you need.

papers/ngram-scoring/2014-Hauer-et-al-So.title: Solving Substitution Ciphers with Combined Language Models
papers/ngram-scoring/2014-Hauer-et-al-So.notes: Combining character- and word-level models. Directly relevant to scoring on a lossy/expanded alphabet where word boundaries are unreliable.

papers/ngram-scoring/2008-Corlett-Penn-A.title: Attacking Decipherment Problems Optimally with Low-Order N-gram Models
papers/ngram-scoring/2008-Corlett-Penn-A.notes: **Important negative-control result:** exact/optimal decipherment under low-order n-gram models, so you can separate 'the search failed' from 'the scoring model cannot see the answer'. The repo's negatives currently cannot make that separation.
